## Purpose

This PR  fixes  #40919  a startup dynamo failure when serving Qwen3.5

`vllm/model_executor/layers/fla/ops/utils.py::input_guard` currently uses:

```python
torch.accelerator.device_index(tensor.device.index)
```

On PyTorch 2.11, Dynamo cannot trace `device_index.__init__` in fullgraph mode, causing engine initialization to fail during the profiling run.

The fix keeps the generic accelerator path for non-CUDA devices (like tpu), but uses the original CUDA-specific context manager for CUDA tensors.

nodes.body: @ProExpertProg @ZJY0516 @vadiklyutiy  could you please have a look at this pr when you have time?

> I removed the `"backend": "eager"` from your command which also uses `dynamo` tor tracing and it works fine. So it's more like a pytorch bug?

Thanks for checking. Yes, this seems specific to `"backend": "eager"`. So this is a bit weird. I’m not sure yet whether this is a PyTorch Dynamo issue or something Bug in vLLM’s compile integration.

@ZJY0516 

Update: I dug further and found this is not specific to backend="eager".

The key difference is the custom-op path. With backend="inductor", vLLM defaults most custom ops to disabled (`custom_ops` gets `none`), so `RMSNormGated` uses the native path. With backend="eager", custom ops default to enabled, so `RMSNormGated.forward_cuda()` is used and Dynamo traces into

```
 ctx = torch.accelerator.device_index(tensor.device.index)
 ```
 
That is what triggers the Dynamo skiplist error.

we can reproduce the same failure with backend="inductor" by explicitly enabling that custom op:

```
python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-num-seqs 512 --no-enable-prefix-caching --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --no-async-scheduling --compilation-config='{"backend": "inductor", "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops": ["+rms_norm_gated"]}' --speculative_config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --language-model-only 
```

This fails at the same line with:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: Attempted to inline function marked as skipped
```

So the trigger is not the eager backend itself, but whether `rms_norm_gated` dispatches to the custom-op `forward_cuda` path. It's not a Pytorch's bug and default inductor command works because it avoids that path. 

So I think this PR is still needed, or any better ideas ?

I encountered the same `torch.accelerator.device_index` Dynamo failure while running Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 with vLLM v0.24.0 on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB GPU.

A local guard around the call allowed `VLLM_COMPILE` with PIECEWISE CUDA graphs to compile and run successfully.  I also have a focused regression test confirming that `device_index` is not invoked through the failing path during compilation while the input-contiguity behavior remains intact.

The resulting runtime successfully loaded the 122B MoE model at a 200,704-token maximum context and completed real approximately 82K-context requests.  Observed performance was approximately 6,514 prompt tokens/second and 100.7 generation tokens/second with MTP K=2.

I see that this PR currently requires a rebase.  Its CUDA device-context approach appears safer for general multi-GPU use than simply bypassing the context during compilation.  If useful, I can prepare a fresh PR against current `main` using this approach together with the focused regression test.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request updates the device context management in vllm/model_executor/layers/fla/ops/utils.py to use torch.cuda.device for CUDA tensors, addressing potential tracing issues with torch.accelerator. The reviewer recommends extending this logic to support XPU devices as well, ensuring consistent behavior across different hardware backends supported by the module.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The tracing issue with `torch.accelerator.device_index` likely affects all accelerator backends when using `torch.compile`. Since this module also supports XPU (Intel), it is recommended to generalize this fix to use the device-specific context manager for both CUDA and XPU. This ensures consistent behavior and avoids tracing failures on Intel platforms as well.

```suggestion
            if tensor.device.type in ("cuda", "xpu"):
                ctx = getattr(torch, tensor.device.type).device(tensor.device.index)
            else:
                ctx = torch.accelerator.device_index(tensor.device.index)
```

files.patch:
@@ -18,6 +18,7 @@
 import torch
 
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.platforms.interface import get_device_context
 from vllm.triton_utils import triton
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
@@ -107,7 +108,7 @@ def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                     break
 
         if tensor is not None:
-            ctx = torch.accelerator.device_index(tensor.device.index)
+            ctx = get_device_context(tensor.device)
         else:
             ctx = contextlib.nullcontext()

@@ -58,6 +58,17 @@ def get_assigned_physical_gpu_ids() -> list[int] | None:
     return _assigned_physical_gpu_ids
 
 
+def get_device_context(
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> contextlib.AbstractContextManager[Any]:
+    if device.type == "cuda":
+        # torch.accelerator.device_index is generally preferred, but it
+        # will cause a torch.compile Dynamo break issue.
+        # see https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/181540
+        return torch.cuda.device(device.index)
+    return torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index)
+
+
 @functools.cache
 def in_wsl() -> bool:
     # Reference: https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/4071
